sentences.text: Proardea stood approximately 70 cm tall and possessed a body shape very similar to modern herons.
This extinct genus, which includes the species Proardea amissa and Proardea? deschutteri, was described by Lambrecht in 1933.
The type species of the genus is Proardea amissa, which was previously known by the synonyms Ardea amissa and Egretta amissa.
Fossils of Proardea have been found in fragmentary form in Quercy, France, with dated remains from the Late Oligocene at Pech Desse, though the original fossil may date back to the Late Eocene.
Researchers suggest that Proardea may have been a direct ancestor of modern herons and egrets because related genera only appear in the fossil record from the Miocene onwards.
Proardea belongs to the family Ardeidae, and its parent group is the subfamily Ardeinae, which includes true herons and egrets.
It is classified as being closely related to the subfamily Ardeinae.
Proardea lived during the Rupelian stage, approximately 33.9 to 27.3 million years ago.
It is debated whether the Miocene genus Proardeola is synonymous with Proardea, with some researchers suggesting Proardeola walkeri might be identical to Proardea amissa.
